explanation: Use slow and fast pointers to detect a cycle. After they meet, advance one pointer from the head and one from the meeting point at equal speed; their next meeting is the original cycle-entry node. No links or values are changed.
timeComplexity: O(n) time over the distinct reachable nodes. Floyd detection and entry-location scans use O(n) link advances over distinct reachable nodes.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. A fixed number of pointers and a cycle-length counter suffice.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: If a cycle exists, the fast pointer gains one position per iteration on the slow pointer modulo the cycle length, so they eventually meet. Let the noncyclic prefix length be μ; the meeting equation implies that advancing one pointer from the head and one from the meeting point reaches the cycle entry together after μ steps. A null fast pointer proves acyclicity.
walkthrough: For values [11,7,4,9], the EPI test setup connects the tail to the original node whose Data is 7 (at zero-based position 1). The cycle is 7→4→9→7. Slow and fast meet at 9; restarting one pointer at 11 makes both next reach the original node 7, which is returned. The executable case’s true result is the judge adapter verdict; the callable returns the tree/node/list of moves/random sample described above.
edgeCases: Return the original entry node, not a copy with the same value.
An acyclic list returns null and no input link may change.
